reason: The passage demonstrates the opposite principle. It depicts Pharaoh as a leader who repeatedly refuses to acknowledge criticism and warnings from Moses and Aaron. Despite witnessing devastating plagues and even confessing sin (וַיֹּ֜אמֶר חָטָ֛אתִי), Pharaoh hardens his heart and renews his resistance rather than accepting correction. His refusal to be humble in the face of these dire warnings leads to escalating national catastrophe, culminating in the death of the firstborn. The text emphasizes God hardening Pharaoh's heart to prevent repentance (וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה). Conversely, Moses and Aaron obediently execute God's will without documented resistance to direction. The narrative presents stubbornness and refusal to accept legitimate correction as the mark of failed leadership, not humility.
